importance_ranking.reason: High visual variation across sub-types (single-storey GI sheet hutment vs double-storey PUF panel colony vs container-based camp) — buyers use the image to immediately identify the construction type, storey count, and finish quality before reading any text. Wrong product type shown = immediate skip for an EPC contractor with a specific site requirement.

Wall panel material, number of floors, and built type are primary shortlisting criteria for EPC and contractor buyers who have project-specific structural and insulation requirements — listings without these specs cannot be evaluated against project tender specifications.

Price varies substantially with wall panel material (GI sheet vs PUF vs Aerocon), storey count, and service inclusions (bare supply vs turnkey) — Indian EPC buyers compare per-sq-ft rates across sellers but only after confirming spec equivalence; price is a primary shortlisting lever once specs match.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Individual room/module orders may be quoted per unit or per room; container-based camps quoted per container — unit must be shown to prevent price comparison errors across these sub-segments.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per unit vs per room creates genuine price comparison confusion for buyers comparing turnkey colony quotes against modular room supply quotes — unit must be displayed alongside price to make comparisons meaningful.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall in this category — market is fragmented across regional fabricators and EPC subcontractors; buyers search by spec, capacity, and price rather than manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: EPC contractors and government project buyers evaluate manufacturer track record, past project references, and installation capability during vendor selection — company credentials matter but only after spec and price shortlisting.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Wall panel material (GI sheet vs PUF panel vs EPS panel vs Rockwool vs Cement Board) defines the insulation grade, durability tier, and thermal comfort of the colony — non-interchangeable across project climate and specification requirements, with a significant price delta between basic PPGI sheet and insulated PUF/Rockwool panels.

Storey count (G vs G+1 vs G+2 vs G+3) determines structural complexity, foundation requirements, and total accommodation capacity — non-interchangeable for a given site footprint and worker headcount, with a substantial price increase per additional floor.

missing_important_specs.why_important: EPC and contractor buyers size their colony order by worker headcount or number of rooms — this is the primary project sizing parameter that determines total order value and seller feasibility to supply.
Turnkey colony pricing is quoted per sq ft of built-up area — buyers and sellers need total area to compare quotes and confirm project scope alignment.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Wall material defines the insulation grade, durability, and compliance tier of the colony — sellers need this to confirm they can supply the specified panel type and to price the order accurately.

Storey count determines structural complexity and total accommodation capacity — sellers need this to assess fabrication feasibility, foundation requirements, and to provide an accurate per-sq-ft quote.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers cannot determine project scale, material quantity, or supply feasibility without knowing the total number of rooms or workers to be accommodated — this is the primary order-sizing parameter.

buyer_spec_audit.image_upload_reason: EPC contractors and government project buyers frequently have site layout drawings, architectural sketches, or reference colony photographs that define the spatial arrangement, storey configuration, and facility inclusions required — an uploaded image or layout plan allows sellers to assess site-specific feasibility and provide a more accurate turnkey quote without multiple back-and-forth clarification rounds.
